# Item

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Short lists such as users or settings, each with a few actions. Not for records analysts compare; those go in a table.

- **Use it when:** Lists of things such as people, files or settings, each with a few actions.
- **Not when:** Records people compare cell by cell (a table).

Instead:

- [Card](./card.md): A larger unit with more content.
- [Table](./table.md): Records compared across columns.

## Why it works this way

Item looks the way it does because of 6 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Item, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-content-q1"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the main content?</b><code>content.q1</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Numbers and records</div><p>Most of the screen is numbers and records.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: Users and settings in a panel or menu, with no border, quiet beside the data.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>outline</b>: Borders on every row would compete with the data; hairlines between sections do that work.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Badge: neutral</code> <code>Badge: info</code> <code>Badge: success</code> <code>Badge: warning</code> <code>Badge: danger</code> <code>Sidebar: default</code> <code>Sidebar: outline</code> <code>Empty: default</code> <code>Toggle: default</code> <code>Toggle: outline</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">5</div><small>Item decisions would reopen</small><p>and 44 answers that follow from it: <b>A lot</b>, <b>Scan and compare</b>, <b>People keep their place</b>, and 41 more.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-elevation-definition"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What separates groups on the page?</b><code>elevation.definition</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Lines</div><p>Thin lines guide the eye along rows.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>outline</b>: Borders on every row would compete with the data; hairlines between sections do that work.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Item decision would reopen</small><p>and 3 answers that follow from it: <b>Only what floats</b>, <b>One</b>, <b>Menus and dialogs</b>.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-tasks-q1"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the main task?</b><code>tasks.q1</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Scan and compare</div><p>People scan rows and compare values.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>muted</b>: The current user or setting, with a soft fill so people keep their place.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Field: vertical</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">4</div><small>Item decisions would reopen</small><p>and 20 answers that follow from it: <b>People keep their place</b>, <b>Acting on the wrong record</b>, <b>Core and data</b>, and 17 more.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-human-q1"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What must the interface protect?</b><code>human.q1</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">People keep their place</div><p>Losing your place in a long table costs time and errors.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>muted</b>: The current user or setting, with a soft fill so people keep their place.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Item decisions would reopen</small><p>and 8 answers that follow from it: <b>Lines</b>, <b>Feedback only</b>, <b>One</b>, and 5 more.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add item
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
